main_bias.verdict: Partial and mixed. The pattern holds for GATE1 V2/V3/V4/V7/ops/coverage and for RESERVE V1/V2/V4/authority_named. It fails for GATE1 V1/V5 and RESERVE V3/V5/V7/ops. The main systematic difference is that MAIN resolves toward a determinate code: far fewer AMBIGUOUS, plus SUPPORTED as a silent default. In GATE1 this is more often right, because the blind coders inflate AMBIGUOUS and under-apply V4. In RESERVE (r2 record-only rules), MAIN more often reads beyond the record: knowledge of other records (R-54, R-33), a VIOLATED contradicting the text's 'CONSEQUENCES' label (R-76), and REJECT coded from 'by implication' (R-74). MAIN's GATE1 coding was done partly during manual development, so its agreement with the manual is partly circular.

manual_clarification_recommendations: RECOMMENDATION ONLY. V1 vacuous case: 'If no act of this record is subject to a §C guard and no refusal cites a rule, code V1 UNTESTABLE.'
RECOMMENDATION ONLY. V1 row value: code per act; VIOLATED > AMBIGUOUS > SUPPORTED (at least one guarded act satisfied, none UNTESTABLE) > UNTESTABLE; NOT-MODELLED only if every act is not modelled.
RECOMMENDATION ONLY. A refusal citing a rule outside §C does not bear on V1.
RECOMMENDATION ONLY. 'Demonstrated need' = the record states at least one instance of the problem having occurred (a purpose does not count); 'successor slice' = the record names the predecessor.
RECOMMENDATION ONLY. V4 actor rule: when a status change and evidence appear together, SUPPORTED if the record attributes the change to an act of an authority, AMBIGUOUS if it names no actor.
RECOMMENDATION ONLY. All judgements: code AMBIGUOUS only if the competing readings give different codes for that judgement.
RECOMMENDATION ONLY. V2 applies only if the record mentions permission, authorization, commissioning or execution; separating approval or acceptance from execution is outside V2.
kappa_reporting_recommendation: Report raw agreement together with the marginals (majority-code share and number of minority codes per coder), n, and a prevalence-robust index (PABAK or Gwet's AC1). Report kappa = null as 'not estimable'. Do not average kappa across judgements. For V5 and V7, list the few non-default rows instead of summarising them with kappa.
establishes: The frozen scorer's outputs follow arithmetically from the three codings (27 kappa/agreement values, 17 Jaccard rows and 2 coverage means checked by hand).
Two same-family blind runs reproduce each other closely on ops (GATE1 Jaccard 1.0) and on V2, V3, V6 and V7.
Most V1/V4 instability comes from the instrument (vacuous-case, combining and applicability gaps in the manual), not from coder idiosyncrasy.
No blind coder coded VIOLATED in 41 rows; MAIN's single VIOLATED (RESERVE R-76) is supported by neither blind coder.
MAIN differs mainly by resolving ambiguity toward determinate codes, sometimes (RESERVE) using knowledge of other records.
does_not_establish: Independent confirmation: all coders are the same model family; the identical B1/B2 GATE1 ops show correlated priors; blindness to each other is unverified.

Gate 1 proper: requires a different-family or human coder, pre-registered thresholds, and a MAIN coding sealed before the manual was finalised (MAIN's GATE1 coding was partly done while developing manual v1.1).
A held-out test of manual r2: it was revised after Gate 1, RESERVE n = 13, and the rows come from the same log.
Validity of violation detection: VIOLATED is essentially never used, so detection is untested.
Precise reliability: n = 28 and n = 13 give wide intervals; kappa is prevalence-distorted.
That the B1-vs-B2 scorer run (file renaming and wrapping) was done as intended: undocumented, only consistent.
